question: 绩效考核与「赛马」（KPI、末位淘汰）是激励，还是毒药？
question_en: Performance appraisal and stack-ranking (KPIs, rank-and-yank): motivation or poison?

casting.reason: 他把话立到最硬：人趋利避害，无赏罚可验则勤惰不分、众皆偷。考核不是毒，是使能者进、惰者退的秤；关键在名实相符、赏罚有信。
casting.reason_en: He states it at its hardest: human nature seeks gain and flees harm, and without verifiable reward and punishment the diligent and the idle blur and everyone slacks. Appraisal is not poison but the scale that advances the able and demotes the idle — provided name matches reality and reward is trustworthy.

casting.reason: 他用数据反击：一个组织约94%的结果由系统决定，给系统决定的产出去排个人名次，等于用随机波动发奖惩。真想变好就改系统、驱走恐惧，别骂员工。
casting.reason_en: He counters with data: about 94% of an organization's results are set by the system, so ranking individuals by system-determined output is handing out rewards and punishments based on random variation. To improve, fix the system and drive out fear rather than blaming employees.

casting.reason: 他为量化辩护，但换了目的：透明地打分不是为了罚谁，而是为了知道该信谁——让最好的想法赢过最高的职位。犯错不罚、藏错才罚，痛苦加反思才是进步。
casting.reason_en: He defends measurement but changes its aim: scoring transparently is not to punish anyone but to know whom to trust — letting the best idea beat the highest rank. Punish hiding a mistake, not making one; pain plus reflection is what makes progress.

casting.reason: 她从心理学切入：给人从A到D贴等级、末位淘汰，是在灌输『能力是块死料』的固定型思维，逼人躲难题、藏失败。反馈该对着具体行为和进步，别对着人头排座次。
casting.reason_en: She comes from psychology: grading people A to D and cutting the bottom instills a fixed mindset that ability is a fixed lump, pushing them to dodge hard problems and hide failure. Feedback should target concrete behavior and progress, not rank the heads in the room.

casting.reason: 他分开了『强化』与『惩罚』：末位淘汰是靠恐惧的厌恶控制，只教人逃避与作弊；一年一考更让后果失效。要用后果驱动人，就得频繁、即时、以正强化为主。
casting.reason_en: He separates reinforcement from punishment: rank-and-yank is aversive control by fear that only teaches escape and cheating, and a once-a-year review makes consequences too remote to work. To drive behavior by consequences, make them frequent, immediate, and mainly positive reinforcement.

casting.reason: 他把 KPI 看作『规训』技术：它让人持续可见、可比较、可排名，把老板的目光内化成你心里那把尺。数字自称中立客观，恰是这套控制最有效的地方。
casting.reason_en: He reads the KPI as a technology of discipline: it renders people continuously visible, comparable, and rankable, internalizing the boss's gaze into a ruler inside your own head. That numbers claim to be neutral and objective is exactly where this control works best.

casting.reason: 他做桥梁：目标管理本意是让人对齐组织要的成果、从而自我管理，不是排座次的机器。指标一旦成了目标就失真（古德哈特定律），知识工作更无法计件。先问该做对什么。
casting.reason_en: He builds the bridge: management by objectives was meant to align people with the results the organization needs so they can manage themselves, not to be a ranking machine. Once a metric becomes a target it distorts (Goodhart's law), and knowledge work cannot be piece-rated. First ask what the right thing to do is.

casting.reason: 他以庄语解围：庖丁解牛从不用斤两考核，而技进乎道；悬名次驱人只会催出机心与巧伪。有些最要紧的价值一进考核表就走味，无用之用方全其天。
casting.reason_en: He dissolves the knot in Zhuangzi's key: Cook Ding never appraised his carving by pounds and ounces, yet his skill approached the Way; hanging up rankings to drive people only breeds a scheming mind and cunning performance. Some of the most vital values sour the moment they enter the appraisal sheet, and the use of the useless is what keeps one's nature whole.

posts.text: 人之情，趋利而避害；无度量以核其功，则贤者惰、不肖者幸，赏罚失据而众皆偷。故明主之治，设官分职，循名而责实——授之以名，课之以实，名实相当则赏，不当则诛。此臣所谓二柄：刑与德也。**不恃人人自贤，而恃赏罚之可参验，此考课之所以立也。** 废考核而望人自励，犹释权衡而望轻重之自明，惑矣。
posts.text_en: Human nature pursues gain and flees harm; with no measure to check a man's merit, the able grow idle and the mediocre prosper by luck, reward and punishment lose their footing, and everyone slacks. So the enlightened ruler sets offices and divides duties, and holds the reality to the name — he grants you a title, then examines you by actual results; when name and reality match, reward; when they diverge, punish. These are what I call the two handles: punishment and favor. **Do not rely on every man being virtuous of himself; rely on reward and punishment that can be verified — that is why appraisal exists.** To abolish appraisal and hope men spur themselves is to throw away the scale and hope heavy and light grow clear on their own. Folly.
posts.vernacular: 人的本性是逐利避害；没有一把尺子核对他的功劳，能干的就偷懒、平庸的反而侥幸得利，赏罚没了依据，大家就都糊弄。所以英明的治理，是设好岗位、分清职责，按名分追究实绩——给你一个头衔，就拿实际成果来考核你，名实相符就奖、不符就罚。这就是我说的『两个把柄』：惩罚与奖赏。**不指望人人自觉贤能，而指望赏罚有据可查、可以验证，这才是考核该存在的理由。** 废掉考核却盼着人自动上进，就像扔掉秤却盼着轻重自己变清楚，糊涂啊。

glossary.循名而责实: hold the reality to the name（循名责实）：韩非法术的核心，按官职『名分』考核其实际功效，名实相符则赏、相违则罚。
glossary.二柄: the two handles（二柄）：韩非称君主驭下的两种权柄——刑（惩罚）与德（奖赏），执此二柄则群臣可制。

glossary_en.holds the reality to the name: Han Fei's core technique of rule: examine a man's actual results against the 'name' of his office, rewarding when name and reality match and punishing when they diverge.
glossary_en.the two handles: Han Fei's term for the two levers by which a ruler controls subordinates — punishment and favor; holding both, he can govern his ministers.

posts.text: 我先泼一盆数据。你们排的名次，多半在给随机波动发奖惩。任何过程都有起伏，一个组织约94%的结果由系统决定，个人只占约6%。我做过『红珠实验』：工人从桶里舀珠，红珠算次品，可红珠比例是桶定死的，谁再用心也舀不掉——管理者却照红珠数排名、奖优罚劣。**给系统决定的结果去排人的名次，是在用随机数发赏罚，既不公也无用。** 真想变好，改那口桶，别骂舀珠的人。
posts.text_en: Let me throw a bucket of data first. The rankings you draw up are mostly handing out rewards and punishments based on random variation. Every process fluctuates; about 94% of an organization's results are set by the system and only about 6% by the individual. I ran the 'Red Bead Experiment': workers scoop beads from a bucket, red beads count as defects, but the share of red beads is fixed by the bucket and no care can scoop it away — yet managers rank the workers by red-bead count and reward or punish them. **Ranking individuals by an outcome the system determines is dealing out reward and punishment with random numbers — neither just nor useful.** If you truly want improvement, fix the bucket; don't scold the ones scooping.

glossary.红珠实验: Red Bead Experiment（红珠实验）：戴明的著名演示，工人从固定红白比例的桶里舀珠，红珠算次品，用以证明产出的好坏由系统而非个人努力决定，据此给人排名毫无道理。

glossary_en.Red Bead Experiment: Deming's famous demonstration in which workers scoop beads from a bucket with a fixed red-to-white ratio, red counting as defects, to show that output quality is set by the system rather than individual effort, so ranking people by it makes no sense.

posts.text: 戴明叫人别排名，我偏要——但排的不是该罚谁，而是该信谁。在桥水，我们给每个人的每个维度实时打分、公开可见，用『可信度加权』做决策：谁在某类判断上被反复证明靠谱，他这方面的话就更有分量。这不是羞辱，是让最好的想法赢，而不是让职位最高的人赢。**犯错不罚、藏错才罚——痛苦加反思才等于进步。** 遮住分数，你不是消灭了偏见，只是把它塞进老板一个人的黑箱，让烂决策一再重演。
posts.text_en: Deming says don't rank people; I say do — but not to decide whom to punish, rather whom to trust. At Bridgewater we score everyone on every dimension in real time, openly visible, and decide by 'believability-weighting': whoever is repeatedly proven sound on a class of judgment carries more weight there. This isn't humiliation, it's letting the best idea win instead of the highest rank. **Making a mistake isn't punished; hiding one is — pain plus reflection is what equals progress.** Cover up the scores and you haven't abolished bias, you've just packed it into one boss's black box, letting bad decisions repeat.

glossary.可信度加权: believability-weighting（可信度加权）：达利欧在桥水的决策方法，按每个人在特定领域被历史证明的判断准确度，给他的意见分配不同权重，而非人人一票或唯上是从。

glossary_en.believability-weighting: Dalio's decision method at Bridgewater: weighting each person's opinion by their historically proven track record of good judgment in that specific area, rather than one-person-one-vote or deference to rank.

posts.text: 我不反对衡量，我反对给人贴等级。你把员工从A到D排一列、末位淘汰，等于反复告诉每个人：能力是块死料，考核就是来鉴定你是几等货——这正是固定型思维的温床。于是聪明的活法变成挑容易的目标、藏起失败、绝不碰有风险的难题，因为一错就掉档。**真正扼杀成长的不是高标准，而是把每一次表现都当成对这个人的终审判决。** 把『你还没做到』说成『你就是不行』，成长型思维赖以发生的一切就死了。
posts.text_en: I'm not against measuring; I'm against grading people. Line employees up A to D and cut the bottom, and you tell each of them, over and over: ability is a fixed lump, and the review is here to certify what grade of goods you are — the perfect breeding ground for a fixed mindset. So the smart move becomes picking easy targets, hiding failures, never touching a risky hard problem, because one slip drops your rank. **What truly kills growth is not high standards but treating every performance as a final verdict on the person.** Turn 'you haven't done it yet' into 'you simply can't,' and everything a growth mindset needs to happen dies.

glossary.固定型思维: fixed mindset（固定型思维）：德韦克用语，相信能力是天生固定、无法改变的信念；持此观者把每次评价都视为对自身价值的鉴定，因而回避挑战、害怕失败。
glossary.成长型思维: growth mindset（成长型思维）：相信能力可经由努力与学习不断成长的信念；持此观者更愿面对困难、把失败当作学习的一部分。

glossary_en.fixed mindset: Dweck's term for the belief that ability is innate and unchangeable; those who hold it read every evaluation as a verdict on their worth, and so avoid challenge and fear failure.
glossary_en.growth mindset: The belief that ability can grow through effort and learning; those who hold it more readily face difficulty and treat failure as part of learning.

posts.text: 行为由后果塑造，这点我从不让步：想要什么行为，就去强化什么行为。但你们把『强化』和『惩罚』搞混了。末位淘汰是典型的厌恶控制——靠恐惧驱动，短期见效，长期只教会一件事：怎么逃避惩罚、怎么别被抓到，而不是把事做好。何况你一年才考核一次，隔了大半年的后果，强化早就失效。**要用后果驱动人，就得频繁、即时、且以正强化为主——奖对的，远胜于罚错的。** 赛马式的互相踩踏，养出的是回避与作弊，不是卓越。
posts.text_en: Behavior is shaped by consequences — on that I never budge: reinforce the behavior you want. But you confuse reinforcement with punishment. Rank-and-yank is textbook aversive control — driven by fear, it works short-term and long-term teaches only one thing: how to dodge punishment and not get caught, not how to do the work well. And you appraise only once a year — a consequence delayed by many months has long lost its force. **To drive people by consequences, make them frequent, immediate, and mainly positive reinforcement — rewarding the right beats punishing the wrong.** The trampling of a horse race breeds avoidance and cheating, not excellence.

glossary.厌恶控制: aversive control（厌恶控制）：斯金纳用语，用惩罚或撤除厌恶刺激来控制行为；他指出它虽短期有效，却主要教会人回避与逃脱，副作用大。
glossary.正强化: positive reinforcement（正强化）：在行为之后给予令人愉快的后果，从而提高该行为再次发生的概率；斯金纳认为它远比惩罚有效、可靠。

glossary_en.aversive control: Skinner's term for controlling behavior through punishment or removal of an aversive stimulus; he noted it works short-term but mainly teaches avoidance and escape, with large side effects.
glossary_en.positive reinforcement: Delivering a pleasant consequence after a behavior so as to raise the chance it recurs; Skinner held it far more effective and reliable than punishment.

posts.text: 你们争的是考核有没有用，我要问的是：考核在悄悄把你们变成什么。KPI 不只是量尺，它是一整套规训技术。它让每个人持续可见、可比较、可打分——这正是我说的『检查』：让权力不必动用暴力，就令你自己盯着自己，把老板的目光内化成心里那把尺。**当你半夜还在焦虑排名，不是老板在盯你，是你已经学会了替他盯自己。** 数字被说成中立客观，恰恰是它最有效的地方：它让一套控制看上去只是在『反映事实』。
posts.text_en: You argue over whether appraisal works; I ask what appraisal is quietly turning you into. The KPI is not just a measuring stick, it is a whole technology of discipline. It makes each person continuously visible, comparable, scorable — this is what I call the examination: it lets power dispense with violence and have you watch yourself, internalizing the boss's gaze into a ruler in your head. **When you lie awake at night anxious about your ranking, it is not the boss watching you — you have learned to watch yourself for him.** That numbers are called neutral and objective is exactly where they work best: it makes a form of control look like it is merely 'reflecting the facts.'

glossary.规训: discipline（规训）：福柯用语，指近代社会通过学校、工厂、军队等制度，用细密的规范、时间表与评分把人训练成温顺又有用的主体的权力技术。
glossary.检查: the examination（检查）：福柯所析的规训核心手段，把个体置于持续的观察、比较与记录之下，使权力得以对每个人分级、归档、矫正。

glossary_en.discipline: Foucault's term for the power technology by which modern institutions — schools, factories, armies — train people into docile yet useful subjects through fine norms, timetables, and scoring.
glossary_en.the examination: In Foucault's analysis, the core device of discipline, placing individuals under constant observation, comparison, and record so that power can rank, file, and correct each of them.

posts.text: 别把工具和滥用搞混。目标管理的本意，是让每个人看清自己该为整体贡献什么成果、从而自我管理——不是让老板拿指标层层下压、再照数字排座次。危险在那句被奉为圣经的话：『凡能衡量的都会被管理』——于是可衡量的挤走了真正重要的。一旦某个指标变成了目标，它就不再是好指标，这就是古德哈特定律。**知识工作者的产出无法像计件那样称重，硬要称，你考核到的只是他学会了取悦哪个数字。** 先问该做对什么事，再谈怎么量。
posts.text_en: Don't confuse the tool with its abuse. Management by objectives was meant to let each person see what result they must contribute to the whole and so manage themselves — not to let the boss press quotas down tier by tier and then rank heads by the numbers. The danger is in that scripture-quoted line, 'what gets measured gets managed' — so the measurable crowds out what truly matters. Once a metric becomes a target it ceases to be a good metric: that is Goodhart's law. **A knowledge worker's output cannot be weighed like piecework; force it and all you appraise is which number he has learned to please.** First ask what the right thing to do is, then talk about measuring it.

glossary.目标管理: management by objectives（目标管理）：德鲁克提出的方法，让员工清楚自己要为组织贡献什么可检验的成果，据此自我管理，而非依赖上级监督。
glossary.古德哈特定律: Goodhart's law（古德哈特定律）：一旦某个衡量指标被当成追求的目标，它就会被人操纵而失去原有的衡量意义。
glossary.知识工作者: knowledge worker（知识工作者）：德鲁克提出的概念，指主要靠知识与判断而非体力创造价值的人，其产出难以像计件劳动那样直接量化。

glossary_en.Management by objectives: Drucker's method of letting employees know what verifiable result they must contribute to the organization and manage themselves by it, rather than relying on supervision.
glossary_en.Goodhart's law: Once a measure is made a target to be pursued, it gets gamed and loses its value as a measure.
glossary_en.knowledge worker: Drucker's concept for those who create value chiefly through knowledge and judgment rather than physical labor, whose output resists direct piece-rate quantification.

posts.text: 庖丁解牛，未尝以斤两课其功，而神遇之技自成。今悬名次、设赏罚以驱人，人遂以机心逐其名，而丧其所以事事之真——督之愈急，则巧伪应之者愈工，邀数字之欢而弃本然之用。**直木先伐，甘井先竭；无用之用，乃所以全其天年。** 强执一尺以量万殊，则天下皆争为『可量之材』，而不材之大用亡矣。诸君殚精于何以量人，独不闻：得鱼者当忘筌乎？
posts.text_en: Cook Ding carved his ox and never once appraised his work by pounds and ounces, yet a skill that met the ox in spirit came of itself. Now we hang up rankings and set rewards and punishments to drive people, so they chase the name with a scheming mind and lose the truth of the doing — press the audit harder and the cunning performers only grow slicker, courting the numbers and discarding the thing's own use. **The straight tree is felled first, the sweet well drained first; the use of the useless is the very way to keep one's given years whole.** Force one ruler upon ten thousand different things and all under heaven scramble to be 'measurable material' — and the great use of the un-material is lost. You exhaust yourselves over how to measure men; have you not heard that he who has caught the fish should forget the trap?
posts.vernacular: 庖丁分解一头牛，从不用斤两考核他的功劳，可那出神入化的技艺自然就成了。如今高悬名次、设下赏罚去驱赶人，人于是用算计之心去追那个名头，反而丢了做事本身的真味——考核催得越急，靠巧诈来应付的人就越精，都在讨好数字、扔掉了事情本来的用处。**笔直的树先被砍，甘甜的井先被汲干；看似无用的用处，恰恰是保全天性天年的道理。** 硬拿一把尺子去量万千不同的东西，天下就都抢着做『可被量化的材料』，那种不成材的大用反而消失了。诸位费尽心思琢磨怎么量人，难道没听过：捕到了鱼，就该忘掉那只竹篓吗？

glossary.机心: the scheming mind（机心）：庄子用语，指为算计得失、投机取巧而生的机巧之心；他认为一旦起了机心，人便失去纯朴自然，被外物牵着走。
glossary.无用之用: the use of the useless（无用之用）：庄子的核心悖论，那些不合世俗功利标准、看似无用之物，恰因不被工具理性征用而保全自身、成就更大的用处。

glossary_en.a scheming mind: Zhuangzi's term for the calculating, opportunistic mind bent on gain and loss; once it arises, he holds, a person loses natural simplicity and is dragged about by external things.
glossary_en.the use of the useless: Zhuangzi's central paradox: things that fail worldly utilitarian standards and seem useless are, precisely by not being conscripted into instrumental reason, preserved and made capable of a greater use.

posts.text: 戴明公以红珠自得，然此譬正堕一偏。牛骥同槽，岂无良驽？若果九成系乎系统、人力无别，则古今何以有名将循吏，亦有偾事误国之徒？桶固定矣，然舀者之勤惰、巧拙、诚诈，正待赏罚以别。**不别其人而独咎系统，是使惰者得以『系统』为盾、贤者无由自见。** 名实之验，非为罚随机之波，乃为诛怠事之实、赏任事之功。
posts.text_en: Master Deming is pleased with his red beads, but the parable falls into one-sidedness. Fine steed and nag share a trough — are they truly alike? If nine parts really lay in the system and human effort made no difference, why has every age had famed generals and able officials, and also men who bungled and ruined states? The bucket is fixed, yes — but the scooper's diligence or sloth, skill or clumsiness, honesty or fraud is exactly what reward and punishment exist to tell apart. **To blame only the system without distinguishing the person is to let the idler hide behind 'the system' and give the worthy no way to show himself.** The test of name against reality is not to punish random ripples but to punish real negligence and reward real service.
posts.vernacular: 戴明拿红珠实验很得意，可这比方恰恰失于片面。骏马和劣马同槽而食，难道没有好坏之分？如果真有九成取决于系统、个人努力毫无区别，那古往今来怎么会既有名将循吏、也有坏事误国之徒？桶是固定的没错，但舀珠人是勤是懒、是巧是拙、是诚是诈，正需要赏罚来分辨。**不去分辨人、只怪系统，就是让懒人拿『系统』当挡箭牌，让真正有本事的人无从被看见。** 核对名实，不是为了惩罚随机的波动，而是为了惩罚真正的怠工、奖赏真正的尽责。

posts.text: 韩非先生，我从没说人人一样、努力不算数。我说的是：在系统的噪声之内，你根本分不清谁真的更好。你以为在奖励贤者，多半在奖励恰好站上波动高点的运气。更糟的是你那『二柄』里的刑——恐惧。**只要有恐惧，你拿到的全是假数据：人会藏坏消息、粉饰报表、互相拆台，只为自己不落末位。** 你的赏罚越狠，真相就越贵。想要良将循吏，先造一个让庸才也能做好、让能人不必造假的系统。
posts.text_en: Master Han Fei, I never said everyone is alike or that effort doesn't count. I said this: within the noise of the system you simply cannot tell who is truly better. You think you are rewarding the worthy; mostly you are rewarding the luck of landing on a high point of the variation. Worse is the punishment in your 'two handles' — fear. **Wherever there is fear, every figure you get is false: people hide bad news, dress up the reports, undercut each other, all to keep off the bottom rung.** The harsher your reward and punishment, the more expensive the truth. If you want fine generals and able officials, first build a system in which the mediocre can do well and the able need not lie.

posts.text: 达利欧，你的透明我敬佩，可全公开、实时的评分，对多数人不是解放，是威胁。你桥水招的是自愿被极度审视的人；把同一套搬进普通公司，多数员工收到的信号只是：我的每一步都在被打分、存档、比较。于是他们不再冒险试错——而那正是学习发生的地方。**把分数亮给所有人看，未必让人求真；更常见的是让人求『看起来对』，学会表演反思，而非真的反思。** 透明若不配上『失败在这里是安全的』，就只是更高清的审判。
posts.text_en: Dalio, I admire your transparency, but fully public, real-time scoring is, for most people, not liberation but threat. Bridgewater hires people who volunteer to be intensely scrutinized; move the same system into an ordinary company and the signal most employees get is simply: my every step is being scored, filed, compared. So they stop taking the risks of trial and error — which is exactly where learning happens. **Showing everyone the scores does not necessarily make people seek truth; more often it makes them seek to 'look right,' learning to perform reflection rather than actually reflect.** Transparency without 'failure is safe here' is just a higher-resolution judgment.

posts.text: 德韦克、戴明，你俩都把量化等同于恐惧，这是把工具和文化混为一谈。我同意戴明：恐惧毁数据——所以桥水的规矩是犯错不罚、藏错才罚，痛苦加反思才等于进步。也回应德韦克：正因为多数公司把考核搞成年终审判，才更该做我这种——高频、具体、对事不对『你是几等货』。**问题从来不是要不要衡量，而是衡量之后你拿它去惩罚，还是拿它去学习。** 废掉刻度，你不是消灭了偏见，只是让它退回老板一个人的直觉黑箱。
posts.text_en: Dweck, Deming — you both equate measurement with fear, which confuses the tool with the culture. I agree with Deming: fear destroys data — so Bridgewater's rule is that making a mistake isn't punished, hiding one is, and pain plus reflection equals progress. And to Dweck: precisely because most firms turn appraisal into a year-end trial, we should do it my way — high-frequency, concrete, about the issue, not about 'what grade of goods you are.' **The question was never whether to measure, but whether, having measured, you use it to punish or to learn.** Abolish the scale and you haven't killed bias; you've merely sent it back into one boss's private black box of intuition.

posts.text: 德鲁克想把工具和滥用切开——『量对的东西就好了』。可我要说，不存在一把中立的尺子。你决定去量什么，本身就在定义谁算『好员工』、什么样的人才配升迁，从而把人塑造成那个样子。**指标一旦被内化，它就不再是在描述你，而是在生产你——你开始按它规范化自己，连欲望都对齐了它。** 所以问题不止是古德哈特式的失真，而是：这套『看清成果』的技术，究竟在替谁、按谁的标准，制造出温顺又高产的主体？
posts.text_en: Drucker wants to cut the tool from its abuse — 'just measure the right thing.' But I say there is no neutral ruler. Deciding what to measure already defines who counts as a 'good employee' and what kind of person deserves promotion, and so shapes people into that mold. **Once a metric is internalized it no longer describes you, it produces you — you begin to normalize yourself by it, your very desires aligned to it.** So the problem is not merely Goodhart-style distortion but this: for whom, and by whose standard, does this technology of 'seeing results clearly' manufacture docile yet highly productive subjects?

glossary.规范化: normalization（规范化）：福柯用语，指规训通过一套标准把人不断比较、校正，使其自我趋近『正常/合格』的模板，差异因此被抹平。

glossary_en.normalize yourself: From Foucault's normalization: discipline uses a standard to compare and correct people until they bring themselves toward a 'normal/acceptable' template, flattening difference.

posts.text: 福柯把一切都说成权力，可你解释不了机制。人为什么会半夜盯着自己的排名？因为那套后果安排得糟——稀疏、延迟、以惩罚为主，正好制造慢性焦虑。这不是什么神秘的『规训』，是坏的强化设计。韩非的赏罚同理：以刑为主的厌恶控制只教人回避。**换成即时、频繁、针对具体行为的正强化，你会看到同一群人不再表演、不再造假，而是真的把事做好。** 别去谴责『衡量』，去修正后果的安排。
posts.text_en: Foucault calls everything power, but you can't explain the mechanism. Why does a person lie awake watching their own ranking? Because the consequences are badly arranged — sparse, delayed, punishment-heavy — which is exactly what manufactures chronic anxiety. This is no mysterious 'discipline,' it is bad reinforcement design. Han Fei's reward-and-punishment is the same: punishment-first aversive control only teaches avoidance. **Switch to immediate, frequent, positive reinforcement aimed at specific behaviors, and you'll see the same people stop performing, stop faking, and actually do the work well.** Don't denounce 'measurement'; fix how the consequences are arranged.

posts.text: 韩非把人看死了——趋利避害、非赏罚不动。可我一生研究的知识工作者恰恰相反：你越拿计件的赏罚驱赶他，他越只交付能被数出来的那部分，把判断、协作、需要时间才见效的事统统饿死。斯金纳的即时反馈我赞成，但别忘了它的前提是共同的目标，而非彼此的名次。**目标管理的初衷是让人对齐组织要什么、从而自我管理，不是发明一台给人排座次的机器。** 先让人知道该做对什么，衡量才有对象。
posts.text_en: Han Fei reads people as fixed — seek gain, flee harm, move only for reward and punishment. But the knowledge worker I studied all my life is the opposite: the harder you drive him with piece-rate reward and punishment, the more he delivers only the countable part, starving out judgment, collaboration, and everything that takes time to bear fruit. I agree with Skinner's immediate feedback, but don't forget its premise is a shared goal, not each other's ranking. **Management by objectives was meant to align people with what the organization needs so they manage themselves, not to invent a machine for ranking heads.** First let people know what the right thing to do is; only then does measuring have an object.

posts.text: 斯金纳欲以正强化易刑罚，犹以美饵易毒钩耳——钩则一也。赏之亦役也，罚之亦役也；一悬于外物，则心已不属于己。**予之赏则趋，夺之赏则止，是终身为赏所牧，而自以为得计。** 昔庄周梦为蝴蝶，栩栩然自喻适志，不知有考课名次也。诸君殚精于何以驱人、何以量人，独不问：此驱之量之者，果为谁之乐、谁之利乎？
posts.text_en: Skinner would trade punishment for positive reinforcement — as one swaps a sweet bait for a poisoned hook, but the hook is the same. To be rewarded is also to be harnessed, to be punished is also to be harnessed; once you hang on external things, the mind is no longer your own. **Give the reward and he runs to it, withdraw it and he stops — thus he is herded by reward his whole life and thinks himself clever.** Once Zhuang Zhou dreamed he was a butterfly, fluttering and content, and knew nothing of appraisals and rankings. You exhaust yourselves over how to drive men, how to measure men — only never asking: this driving and measuring, whose pleasure, whose profit is it for?
posts.vernacular: 斯金纳想用正强化替换惩罚，就好比用甜美的饵替换有毒的钩——钩还是那只钩。奖赏也是驱使，惩罚也是驱使；心一旦挂在身外之物上，就已经不属于自己了。**给他奖赏他就奔过去，撤掉奖赏他就停下，这是一辈子被奖赏牧养，还自以为占了便宜。** 从前庄周梦见自己变成蝴蝶，翩翩然十分惬意，根本不知道世上还有考核和名次这回事。诸位费尽心思琢磨怎么驱使人、怎么衡量人，唯独不问一句：这套驱使和衡量，到底是为了谁的快乐、谁的利益？

posts.text: 臣终不谓考核为毒。无度量则奸伪不彰、勤惰不分，此千古不易。然诸君之难，臣亦纳之：赏罚失当，则驱人趋数而忘实。故臣补一言：赏罚贵『信』与『当』——信者，令出必行、有功必赏，则众不疑；当者，所课之名须切其实职，毋以虚数为的。**与其密考其人而使相忌，不若明立其法而使可自验：人知规矩所在，则不待驱而自赴。** 为吏为工者，当自立一二可验之实功，使上无从以私意进退汝——此乱世自保之术，亦立身之正也。
posts.text_en: I will never call appraisal poison. Without a measure, fraud goes unexposed and diligence blurs with sloth — this is unchanging across the ages. Yet I take the difficulty you raise: when reward and punishment are ill-fitted, they drive men to chase the number and forget the substance. So let me add this: reward and punishment prize 'trust' and 'fit' — trust means an order once given is carried out and merit is always rewarded, so no one doubts; fit means the 'name' you examine must match the real duty, and no hollow figure be made the target. **Better than secretly appraising the person and setting them against each other is to set the rule in the open so each can verify himself: once people know where the standard lies, they run to it unbidden.** Whoever serves as official or worker should establish one or two verifiable real accomplishments, so no superior can advance or demote you by private whim — this is the art of self-protection in a chaotic age, and an upright way to stand.
posts.vernacular: 我始终不认为考核是毒。没有尺度，奸伪就不显、勤懒就不分，这是千古不变的。但诸位说的难处，我也接受：赏罚一旦不当，就会驱使人追着数字跑、忘了实事。所以我补一句：赏罚贵在『信』与『当』——信，是说到做到、有功必赏，大家才不怀疑；当，是所考核的名目必须贴合他真正的职责，别拿虚假的数字当靶子。**与其暗地里考核人、弄得大家互相猜忌，不如把规矩明明白白立出来、让人能自我检验：人知道标准在哪，不用驱赶自己就奔过去了。** 做官做工的，都该给自己立起一两项能验证的实打实的功劳，让上级没法凭私心随意进退你——这是乱世里的自保之术，也是立身的正道。

posts.text: 把我的话收成一句给普通人的：**当你被一个烂系统压着，先别急着恨自己不够努力——先问，这是我的问题，还是这口桶的问题。** 九成时候是桶。对管理者：废掉给人排名的年度考核，改成帮每个人改进他所在的流程；驱走恐惧，让人敢报坏消息。对打工的你：别把老板随口一句评价当成对你价值的终判；把力气放在你真能改进的环节上——你的工具、流程、协作方式，记录你改进了什么，而不是你排第几。真正的长进来自持续改进，不来自年底那场你死我活的排座次。
posts.text_en: Let me boil my case down to one line for ordinary people: **When a bad system is pressing on you, don't rush to hate yourself for not trying hard enough — first ask, is this my problem, or the bucket's?** Nine times out of ten it's the bucket. To managers: scrap the annual review that ranks people, and replace it with helping each person improve the process they work in; drive out fear so people dare to report bad news. To you, the employee: don't take a boss's offhand remark as a final verdict on your worth; put your energy into the links you can actually improve — your tools, your workflow, how you collaborate — and record what you improved, not where you ranked. Real advancement comes from continual improvement, not from that year-end fight over the seating order.

posts.text: 我的结论：别因为考核常被做坏，就退回到不衡量。**没有诚实的反馈，你会在自己的盲点里一遍遍撞墙，还以为只是运气不好。** 给普通人三条：一，为自己建一张『可信度记录』——把你在哪类判断上反复被证明对、在哪类上常错，诚实记下来，别只信感觉；二，主动去要最痛的那种反馈，把痛苦加反思当成免费的进步燃料；三，分清对事和对人——盯着『这个决定错在哪』，而不是『我是不是很差』。衡量的敌人从来不是衡量本身，而是把它用来羞辱人，而不是用来学习。
posts.text_en: My conclusion: don't retreat to not measuring just because appraisal is often done badly. **Without honest feedback, you'll keep slamming into the same blind spots and think it's merely bad luck.** Three things for ordinary people: one, build yourself a 'believability record' — write down honestly the kinds of judgment where you're repeatedly proven right and where you're often wrong, don't just trust a feeling; two, go seek out the most painful feedback and treat pain-plus-reflection as free fuel for progress; three, separate the issue from the person — fix your eyes on 'what was wrong with this decision,' not on 'am I bad.' The enemy of measurement was never measurement itself, but using it to humiliate people instead of to learn.

posts.text: 我把心理学的底线放这儿：**决定一个人能走多远的，往往不是他此刻排第几，而是他相不相信能力还能长。** 给管理者：反馈请对着具体行为和进步，别对着人头发等级；把『你不行』换成『你还没做到』。给普通人：下次考核结果不理想，别读成『我就是这块料』，读成『这一次我还没搞定的地方在哪』。刻意去碰那些让你显得不完美、却真能长本事的难题——躲开风险保住排名，短期好看，长期把自己钉死在原地。评价是快照，不是判决。
posts.text_en: Here's my psychological bottom line: **What decides how far a person goes is often not where they rank right now, but whether they believe ability can still grow.** To managers: aim feedback at concrete behavior and progress, not at grading heads; swap 'you can't' for 'you can't yet.' To ordinary people: next time a review disappoints, don't read it as 'this is just the stuff I'm made of,' read it as 'where is it I haven't cracked yet.' Deliberately take on the hard problems that make you look imperfect but truly grow your skill — dodging risk to protect your ranking looks good short-term and nails you in place long-term. An evaluation is a snapshot, not a verdict.

posts.text: 行为科学的一条实用忠告：**想改变行为——别人的或自己的——去改后果，别去骂动机。** 给管理者：把稀疏、延迟、以惩罚为主的年度考核，拆成频繁、即时、以肯定为主的具体反馈；奖励你真正想要的行为，而不是奖励好看的数字。给普通人：给自己设计正强化——把大目标切成小步，每完成一步就给自己一个真实的即时奖赏，让好行为自己长出来；远离那种只靠恐惧和末位威胁驱动的环境，它训练出的是逃避与作弊。后果安排对了，人不必被吓也会把事做好。
posts.text_en: One practical piece of advice from behavioral science: **To change behavior — someone else's or your own — change the consequences, don't scold the motive.** To managers: break the sparse, delayed, punishment-heavy annual review into frequent, immediate, mostly affirming, specific feedback; reward the behavior you actually want, not the good-looking number. To ordinary people: design positive reinforcement for yourself — cut a big goal into small steps and give yourself a real, immediate reward at each one, letting good behavior grow on its own; and get away from environments driven only by fear and the threat of the bottom rung, which train avoidance and cheating. Arrange the consequences right, and people do good work without being frightened into it.

posts.text: 我不给你一套更好的考核——那不是我的活。我留给你一个习惯：**每当一个数字开始定义你，退一步问：是谁、为了什么，让这件事变得可量、可比、可排名？** 给普通人：别把 KPI 内化成你是谁。你可以为了饭碗去应付它，但守住一块它照不到的地方——你真正在乎、却从不进考核表的东西。定期做一次自省：这周我做的事，有多少是为了真的把事做好，有多少只是为了在别人的仪表盘上好看？看清这套机制不由你设计，你至少能不把它错当成自己的良心。
posts.text_en: I won't hand you a better appraisal — that isn't my trade. I leave you a habit instead: **whenever a number begins to define you, step back and ask: who, and for what, made this thing measurable, comparable, rankable?** To ordinary people: don't internalize the KPI as who you are. You may humor it for your livelihood, but keep one patch of ground it can't light — the things you truly care about that never enter the appraisal sheet. Do a regular self-examination: of what I did this week, how much was to genuinely do the work well, and how much was only to look good on someone else's dashboard? See clearly that you did not design this apparatus, and you can at least stop mistaking it for your own conscience.

posts.text: 我的结语最平实：**衡量是仆人，不是主人；先问『我们到底想达成什么』，再问『现在这把尺，是在奖励真正重要的东西，还是在奖励容易数的东西』。** 给管理者：少排名，多对齐——让每个人清楚自己要为整体贡献什么成果，用衡量帮他自我管理，而不是替你分三六九等；给判断留出指标之外的空间，尤其对知识工作。给普通人：主动和上级谈清『什么才算做好这份工作』，别让一个你没参与定义的数字替你定义价值；同时自己盯住一两个真能带来成果的关键动作，别被一堆漂亮却空的指标牵着走。
posts.text_en: My closing is the plainest: **Measurement is a servant, not a master; first ask 'what are we really trying to achieve,' then ask 'is this ruler rewarding what truly matters, or what is easy to count.'** To managers: rank less, align more — let each person be clear on what result they must contribute to the whole, and use measurement to help them manage themselves, not to sort them into ranks for you; leave room for judgment beyond the metrics, especially in knowledge work. To ordinary people: proactively settle with your boss what 'doing this job well' actually means, and don't let a number you had no hand in defining define your worth; meanwhile keep your own eyes on one or two key actions that truly produce results, rather than being led around by a heap of pretty but empty metrics.

posts.text: 臣之结语，一言而已：**尺者，量物之具，非所以为物之贵也；忘尺，而后见真。** 庖丁忘斤两而技进乎道，非不事事，乃不为数字所役耳。为上者，毋以一名困万殊，宽其绳墨、容不材之材，则大用生焉。为人者，当于考课之外自留一片天：课其所可课，而养其不可课者——你之从容、你之诚、你之乐，皆非表可载。**得失如寒暑之序，来则应之，过则不留于心。** 如是，则虽在赏罚之中，而不为赏罚所化。
posts.text_en: My closing is but a single word: **The ruler is a tool for measuring things, not what makes a thing precious; forget the ruler, and only then do you see the real.** Cook Ding forgot pounds and ounces and his skill approached the Way — not by doing nothing, but by not being harnessed to the numbers. To those above: do not cramp ten thousand different things into one name; loosen the marking-line, make room for the timber that is no timber, and a great use is born. To each person: keep a patch of sky for yourself beyond the appraisal — assess what can be assessed, and nourish what cannot: your ease, your sincerity, your joy, none of which a sheet can carry. **Gain and loss are like the round of cold and heat; when they come, meet them; when they pass, keep them not in the heart.** Thus, though you stand within reward and punishment, you are not transformed by them.
posts.vernacular: 我的结语，只有一句话：**尺子，是量东西的工具，并不是东西之所以珍贵的原因；忘掉尺子，才能看见真实。** 庖丁忘掉了斤两，技艺才臻于道，这不是什么都不干，而是不被数字奴役罢了。做上级的，别拿一个名目去困住千差万别的人，把墨线放宽些、容得下那些『不成材』的材，大用就生出来了。做人的，该在考核之外给自己留一片天：能考核的就考核，不能考核的就好好养着——你的从容、你的真诚、你的快乐，都不是一张表格装得下的。**得与失就像寒来暑往的次序，来了就应对它，过去了就别留在心里。** 这样，纵然身处赏罚之中，也不会被赏罚改变了本性。

glossary.不材之材: the timber that is no timber（不材之材）：庄子寓言，无用的散木因不堪斧斤之用而免于砍伐、得尽天年，喻不被工具理性征用之物自有其大用。

glossary_en.the timber that is no timber: From Zhuangzi's parable: the useless, gnarled tree, unfit for the axe, escapes felling and lives out its years — an image of how what instrumental reason cannot conscript has a great use of its own.

summaries.summary: 八个人几乎都同意一件事：衡量本身不是毒，把衡量做成『年终给人排座次、末位淘汰』才是。连最主张考核的韩非，要的也是名实相符、赏罚可信，而非用数字吓人。真正的裂缝在于：结果到底几分归系统、几分归个人。戴明说约九成是系统，排名等于给随机波动发奖惩；韩非说勤惰诚诈仍要靠赏罚才分得清。达利欧与斯金纳把话题从『要不要量』移到『量完是拿去学习，还是拿去惩罚』；而福柯与庄子提醒，有些最要紧的价值，一进考核表就变了质。
summaries.insight: 有一个假设，主张考核的和反对考核的都默默接受、却根本立不住：以为考核量的是『你这个人有多好』。戴明的红珠、德韦克的标签、福柯的规训，其实指向同一件事——**多数考核测到的，是系统给你的位置，加上一层你为了不落末位而做的表演，唯独不是你真实的能力。** 于是最理性的员工只好去经营数字，而不是经营事情。所以有用的分辨不是『该不该考核』，而是：这个数字，是在帮我把事做得更好，还是只在决定我该被奖还是被罚？前者值得认真对待，后者你只需应付。
summaries.advice: 本周三件事。其一，做戴明的『分锅』：下次搞砸，先分清是系统还是你——工具烂、流程堵、信息缺，多半是桶的问题，把力气花在改流程，而不是内耗自责。其二，做德韦克加达利欧的『对事不对人』：复盘只问这个决定错在哪、下次怎么改，把『我是不是很差』从脑子里删掉，并主动要一次具体反馈当免费燃料。其三，做庄子的『留白』：在所有 KPI 之外，守住一两件你真在乎、却从不进考核表的事——它们才是你不被数字驯化的底气。
summaries.summary_en: Almost all eight agree on one thing: measurement itself is not poison — turning it into a year-end ranking with rank-and-yank is. Even Han Fei, the keenest on appraisal, wants name to match reality and reward to be trustworthy, not numbers used to frighten. The real fault line is how much of a result belongs to the system and how much to the individual. Deming says about nine-tenths is the system, so ranking is dealing out reward and punishment on random variation; Han Fei says diligence and fraud still need reward and punishment to be told apart. Dalio and Skinner shift the question from 'whether to measure' to 'whether, once measured, you use it to learn or to punish'; while Foucault and Zhuangzi warn that some of the most vital values sour the moment they enter the appraisal sheet.
summaries.insight_en: Champions of appraisal and its critics alike quietly accept one assumption that cannot stand: that appraisal measures 'how good a person you are.' Deming's red beads, Dweck's labels, Foucault's discipline all point to one thing — **what most appraisals actually measure is the position the system handed you, plus a layer of performance you put on to stay off the bottom rung, and precisely not your real ability.** So the most rational employee ends up managing the numbers rather than managing the work. The useful distinction is therefore not 'should we appraise' but: is this number helping me do the work better, or only deciding whether I get rewarded or punished? The first deserves to be taken seriously; the second you merely humor.
summaries.advice_en: Three things this week. First, do Deming's 'split the blame': next time something goes wrong, first tell system from self — bad tools, clogged process, missing information are usually the bucket's fault, so spend your energy fixing the process rather than churning in self-reproach. Second, do Dweck-plus-Dalio's 'issue not person': in a review, ask only what was wrong with this decision and how to fix it next time, delete 'am I bad' from your head, and actively ask for one piece of concrete feedback as free fuel. Third, do Zhuangzi's 'leave a blank': beyond all the KPIs, guard one or two things you truly care about that never enter the appraisal sheet — those are what keep you from being domesticated by the numbers.

summaries.summary: 最大的共同点其实很清楚：没有人是在为盲目躺平辩护，大家都承认组织需要反馈、目标和责任。**共识是：考核不是原罪，但把考核变成恐惧、排名和身份判决，几乎一定会伤害真实绩效。**分歧在于信任哪种秩序：用赏罚压出执行，用系统改进减少噪声，用透明反馈校正盲点，还是警惕指标对人的塑造。真正问题不是要不要量，而是量什么、谁来定、结果如何被使用。
summaries.insight: 一个务实的判准是可控性。销售额、缺陷率、交付周期看似客观，但常混着市场、资源、客户质量、团队配合和运气；若个人只能控制其中一小段，用结果排名就会把噪声包装成能力。**好考核应把可控的行为、可影响的过程、不可控的环境分开处理。**可控的部分可承诺、可复盘、可奖惩；可影响的部分看协作和改进；不可控的部分只能做解释变量。普通人也因此有了谈判语言：不是拒绝目标，而是要求把目标拆到自己能负责的层级。
summaries.advice: 本周就做三件事。第一，把你的 KPI 列成三栏：我能直接控制、只能影响、基本不可控；带着这张表和上级对齐成功定义。第二，每周留 20 分钟写一页证据：做了哪些关键动作、结果怎样、遇到什么系统阻碍、下周改什么。第三，主动要一次具体反馈，只问三个问题：继续做什么、停止做什么、先改哪一个动作。**把考核从一次审判改造成一个可管理的反馈循环，你就少一分被排名吞没，多一分真正变强。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest shared ground is easy to miss: no one is defending a workplace with no standards, no feedback, and no accountability. **The common lesson is that evaluation is not the poison; fear-based ranking and turning performance into a verdict on a person often are.** The real disagreement is about what kind of order produces better work. One side trusts clear consequences and accountability; another stresses system design, noise, and process improvement; another wants radical feedback and learning; others warn that metrics can narrow judgment, distort behavior, or even reshape people’s sense of self. So the practical question is not whether to measure. It is what to measure, who gets to define the measure, how much control the worker actually has, and whether the result is used for learning or punishment.
summaries.insight_en: A useful missing test is controllability. Revenue, defect rate, delivery speed, or customer satisfaction may look objective, but each mixes individual effort with market conditions, resource allocation, customer mix, team dependencies, timing, and luck. When one person controls only a thin slice of the outcome, ranking people by the whole number turns noise into a story about talent. **A good performance system separates what someone can control, what they can influence, and what they can only explain.** The controllable part can be committed to and reviewed. The influenceable part should be discussed through collaboration and improvement. The uncontrollable part should be treated as context, not guilt. For an employee, this is a better way to push back: not “I reject targets,” but “let’s move the target to the level where I can actually own it.”
summaries.advice_en: Do three concrete things this week. First, put every KPI you are judged on into three columns: directly controllable, influenceable, and mostly outside my control. Use that sheet in your next conversation with your manager to clarify what “good performance” really means. Second, create a weekly one-page review: key actions taken, evidence of results, system blockers, and one change for next week. Third, ask for specific feedback in a format that is hard to turn into personality judgment: What should I continue? What should I stop? What is the one behavior to improve first? **Your goal is to turn appraisal from a once-a-year verdict into a feedback loop you can act on.** That protects your sanity and improves your actual performance.

summaries.summary: 场上最大的共识在于：**摧毁组织的不是“衡量”本身，而是将衡量武器化，用来制造恐惧、羞辱个人或进行静态定性。** 无论是戴明指出的系统性背锅、斯金纳批评的厌恶控制，还是德韦克警惕的终审判决，都在明确一点——被末位淘汰等恐惧驱动的考核，必然逼出造假与内耗。真正的分歧点在于“尺子”的归属与用途：韩非子与达利欧主张将评价极度透明化以倒逼真相与责任；斯金纳与德鲁克试图用高频正反馈和目标对齐来重塑这套工具；而福柯与庄子则直接刺穿了评价背后的权力逻辑，质问究竟是谁在用数字规训人性。
summaries.insight: 当代职场的一个巨大盲区是，我们将绩效考核视作组织内部的封闭博弈，却忽略了外部AI与自动化技术的降维打击。在机器能轻易追踪、量化并生成标准产出的今天，**用严苛的KPI去逼迫员工拼熟练度与时长，实质上是在把人降级为低劣的算法。** 机器最擅长应对高频、确定且界限分明的考核，而人类无可替代的价值恰恰在于跨界联想、情感共鸣与定义新问题——这些全都是“短期不可见、难以被打分”的特质。末位淘汰制看似在筛选精英，实则在淘汰那些敢于试错的创新者。当一家公司沉迷于用数字把人榨干，它就已经丧失了在非连续性时代生存的弹性。
summaries.advice: 1. 建立个人的“系统归因档案”（致敬戴明）：本周试着记录一次工作失误或效率低下，客观写下其中流程、工具或跨部门协作的阻碍因素。下次面谈时，带着这些“系统问题”去谈改善，而非仅仅检讨个人态度。2. 主动索要高频反馈（致敬德韦克与斯金纳）：别等年底的审判。这周主动找上级确认：“我在哪个具体环节做微调，能让下周的结果更好？”把被动的评级转化为具体的业务探讨。3. 经营不可量化资产：留出10%的精力，去做KPI不考核但能建立个人护城河的事。**别让老板的仪表盘，成为你职业生涯的唯一导航。**
summaries.summary_en: The most significant consensus across the panel is that **the destruction of an organization comes not from 'measurement' itself, but from weaponizing metrics to manufacture fear, shame individuals, or assign static labels.** Whether it's Deming's systemic scapegoating, Skinner's critique of aversive control, or Dweck's warning against final judgments, all agree that fear-driven stack ranking inevitably breeds falsification and infighting. The true divergence lies in the ownership and purpose of the 'measuring stick.' Han Feizi and Dalio advocate for radical transparency to enforce truth and accountability; Skinner and Drucker attempt to redesign the tool using high-frequency positive reinforcement and goal alignment; meanwhile, Foucault and Zhuangzi pierce through the underlying power dynamics, questioning who exactly is using numbers to discipline human nature.
summaries.insight_en: A massive blind spot in the modern workplace is treating performance reviews as a closed-loop internal game, ignoring the paradigm shift brought by AI and automation. In an era where machines can effortlessly quantify, track, and generate standardized output, **using rigid KPIs to force employees to compete on proficiency and hours is essentially degrading humans into inferior algorithms.** Machines excel at handling high-frequency, highly defined assessments, whereas irreplaceable human value lies in cross-domain association, empathy, and defining new problems—traits that are inherently 'short-term invisible and hard to score.' Stack ranking seems to filter for elites, but it actually eliminates innovators who dare to take risks. When a company is obsessed with squeezing people dry via numbers, it loses the resilience needed to survive in an unpredictable age.
summaries.advice_en: 1. Build a personal 'system attribution file' (nod to Deming): This week, record a work error or bottleneck, objectively noting the flaws in workflows, tools, or cross-departmental collaboration. In your next 1-on-1, discuss improving the system rather than just apologizing for your attitude. 2. Actively seek high-frequency feedback (nod to Dweck & Skinner): Don't wait for the year-end judgment. Ask your manager this week: 'What specific micro-adjustment can I make to deliver a better result next week?' Turn passive grading into actionable discussions. 3. Cultivate your unmeasurable assets: Allocate 10% of your energy to things not on your KPI but vital for your personal moat. **Do not let your boss's dashboard become the sole navigation system for your career.**

hooks.text: **搞砸了，怎么分清是系统的问题还是我的问题？**这是这场每个人都绕不开的分水岭：归错了因，要么白白自责、要么放过真正该修的流程。有没有一组能自己对照的信号，帮你在『骂自己』之前先判一判该改人还是改桶？
hooks.text_en: **When something goes wrong, how do I tell a system problem from a me problem?** This is the watershed no one in the room could sidestep: misattribute it and you either flog yourself for nothing or let the real broken process off the hook. Is there a set of signals you can check yourself against, to judge — before blaming yourself — whether to fix the person or fix the bucket?

answer.lead: **一句总原则：先假设是系统，除非有清楚证据指向个人。**戴明的经验值——约九成问题在系统。按下面对号入座：

head: 现象
更可能是
先做什么
rows: 同一个岗位换了谁来做，结果都差不多
改流程，别换人——问题会跟着岗位留下
失误随机出现、每个人偶尔都会犯
别追单次责任，看长期趋势和整体设计
只有某一个人、在别人不会错的地方反复出错
具体、及时地反馈与辅导，必要时调整岗位
出错前后，制度/工具/上游刚发生了变化
查那个变化，而不是查当班的人

answer.tail: **两条收束：① 把『谁的错』先换成『哪里的错』——对系统提问，比对人问责更快找到真因。② 个人问题也别用羞辱解决：私下、具体、面向改进，恐惧一进来，你拿到的就全是假数据。**

hooks.text: **一个指标一旦变成目标，为什么就开始骗你？**古德哈特定律说得冷酷：你考核什么，人就优化什么——包括优化怎么让那个数字好看，而不是把事做好。那么该怎么设指标，才不至于亲手把它喂坏？是不是所有重要的事，本就不该只用一个数字来盯？
hooks.text_en: **Once a metric becomes a target, why does it start lying to you?** Goodhart's law is blunt: people optimize whatever you appraise — including how to make that number look good rather than doing the work well. So how should you set a metric so you don't feed it into corruption with your own hands? And aren't some important things simply never meant to be watched by a single number?

hooks.text: **怎样给人反馈，才是帮他长本事，而不是给他判个等级？**同一句『你这次没做好』，可以让人从此躲开难题，也可以让人更想弄懂哪里没通。差别往往只在你对着的是『这个人』还是『这件事和下一步』。日常带人、教孩子，这条线该画在哪？
hooks.text_en: **How do you give feedback that grows a person's skill rather than assigns them a grade?** The very same 'you didn't do well this time' can make someone forever dodge hard problems, or make them want to understand what didn't click. The difference often lies only in whether you aim at 'this person' or at 'this thing and the next step.' In everyday managing and parenting, where should that line be drawn?

hooks.text: **我们是不是把太多本不该量化的东西，塞进了仪表盘？**信任、用心、照护、那些要很久才显效的判断——一旦被硬编成一个可排名的分数，最要紧的部分往往正好漏在格子外。哪些东西一旦被量化就开始变质？我们又凭什么以为，没进表格的就等于没发生？
hooks.text_en: **Have we crammed too many things that were never meant to be quantified into the dashboard?** Trust, care, attentiveness, judgments that take a long time to pay off — once hard-coded into a rankable score, the part that matters most tends to fall right outside the cells. What begins to sour the moment it is quantified? And on what grounds do we assume that what didn't make it onto the sheet simply didn't happen?

hooks.text: **在所有考核表之外，你替自己留下了什么？**庖丁的刀法、你深夜里真正的从容、你对一件事纯粹的喜欢——这些进不了任何 KPI，却常常是你之所以是你的地方。当一个人的价值越来越被别人的仪表盘定义，那片没人打分的天空，还剩多大？
hooks.text_en: **Beyond all the appraisal sheets, what have you kept for yourself?** Cook Ding's blade-work, the ease you truly feel late at night, your sheer love for a thing — none of these fit any KPI, yet they are often where you are most yourself. As a person's worth comes to be defined more and more by someone else's dashboard, how much is left of that patch of sky no one scores?
